summary:
UNSAFE FOR PILOTS UNTIL THE RENDERER AND HUD ENGINEERS ARE DONE: landing now works end to end on server and client, so a hard ground contact costs hull or the ship, but nothing draws the ground, the base has no model, the HUD shows no height and still says "NORMAL FLIGHT" for a landed ship. From the ground even the body's sphere is gone: the camera is below the mean radius (1335.94 km from the centre of a 1336 km body on the dev page; no limb in the live screenshot at the pad). A pilot cannot land by eye yet.

NOT IN THE REPO AS A TEST: the view wiring in packages/client/src/game/Game.ts (buildView) and packages/client/src/ui/Hud.tsx. The conversion is unit-tested through game/surface.ts and dev/fakeView.ts; buildView and the HUD entries were checked only by a scratch script against the real client (path under verification).

THIS SESSION CHANGED NO FILE. It was a resumed task: all of the work was made between 99a5d2c and b7669b6 by the earlier session of this same role. I read all of it, grepped again for missed entries, re-ran every check on b7669b6 (tree clean before and after), extended the live check to the three HUD entries, and found nothing that called for a code change.

State of b7669b6: tsc clean for all three packages, 542 tests pass (488 baseline + 37 in tests/landing.test.ts + 17 in packages/client/src/game/surface.test.ts), client builds, scripts/e2e.mjs ended "e2e ok" (one run witnessed, two more read from the earlier session's logs), and none of the three logs has the "fold tunnel ... was never seen" warning that the baseline log has on both jumps.

What is now true. Server: ships in surface frames are stepped and are a zone of their own; Landed ships are in the world (detected, locked, hit, rammed, shields work) and cannot fire, mine, salvage, scoop, jettison or charge a drive; hard touchdowns cost hull by a stated rule; wrecks and pods fall and rest, missiles go off at the ground, shots end at the terrain; docking, undocking, trade, missions, home, respawn and insurance work at ground bases; ships collide with the base structure; weapons are locked around a base in secure space; logout and login keep a landed ship where it stood; NPC ships are never in a surface frame. Client: Landed is simulated, predicted and drawn; every position, velocity and orientation in the FrameView is in system axes; the view carries zoneRot and a `surface` block; effects stay on the ground; the chase, docked and wreck cameras stay above the terrain; the handoff shows the fold tunnel; the dev page has a `surface` scene.

Found by the new grep and scan, no change needed: no orbital site lies inside the surface-frame shell of a landable body (0 of 449 such sites in 992 generated systems; the closest periapsis is 108 km above the height where the frame begins and 18 km above the height where it ends). That is what the generator happens to produce, not an enforced rule, and station zones (250 km) do reach into the shell.
behaviour:
HARD LANDINGS (packages/server/src/ground.ts impactFraction, sim.ts groundImpact). v = StepEnv.impact, the m/s by which a contact exceeds the gentle limits (6 m/s sink, 8 m/s sideways). Share of the FULL hull lost = 0.25 * (v / 10)^1.5 * scale. Stock Wisp (scale 1): 25 % at 10 m/s over, 71 % at 20, 100 % at about 25.2. scale = cube root of (mass per hull point / the stock Wisp's), clamped to 0.7..1.6: about 1.5 for a Drover (lost at about 19 to 20 m/s over), about 1.3 for a Bulwark, less with armour. The shields take none of it. One impact lasts until 1 s (IMPACT_EPISODE) has passed without a hard contact; within it only what a harder contact adds is charged, so a bounce or a slide is charged once. The pilots around get a 'hit' event (shield false) at the ground under the ship; a fatal one also gives the notice 'crash'. Bodies that cannot be landed on keep the old rule (notice 'impact', destroyed).

LANDED ON THE SERVER. Zone = the surface anchor (500 + body). Stepped through simulateShip every tick (lift-off, regeneration, signature). Damage, lock, beam and shell hits, missile fuse and missile steering all accept Landed targets. In a ship-to-ship collision the landed ship does not move: the other takes the whole push and bounce, both take the usual damage. It is skipped by the base collider. Refused while landed: fire, mining and salvage laser, scooping, jettison, cruise ('Lift off first.'), fold ('Lift off first.'), giving fuel. Allowed: docking at a base, receiving fuel, survey scan. A drive charge in progress ends at touchdown (notice 'charge_landed'). Flags: EntityFlag.Landed (plus Wanted), never Thrust or Firing. Saved states: Landed is accepted only with a surface anchor, otherwise the pilot returns docked at home.

CRUISE AND FOLD NEAR THE GROUND. A ceiling drop (StepEnv.cruiseDrop) sends 'cruise' off to the cruise layer and to the surface zone and the notice 'cruise_ceiling'. Below the ceiling both drives answer 'Too close to the ground: climb above the cruise ceiling.' (command reply, and notice 'cruise_ground' when a charge completes there).

THINGS ON THE GROUND (sim.ts stepObjects). In a surface zone every object gets vel += accelerationAt(env, pos, vel) * dt (gravity, Coriolis, centrifugal). When its origin comes below terrain + (belly ?? radius) it is set on that height: a pod (radius 2 m) or wreck (the dead ship's belly) gets velocity 0 and `resting`, and never moves again; a missile emits 'hit' (id = the missile's id, dmg = its damage, shield false) there and is removed, with no area damage. Objects in other zones drift in straight lines as before. A ship destroyed flying or landed leaves its wreck with the cargo; the wreck starts with the ship's last velocity.

SHOTS (ground.ts groundRay, used by weapons.ts trace). In a surface zone a shot ends at the terrain: nothing is sampled when the whole segment is above the highest ground of the body; otherwise at most 48 steps of half the height above ground (4 to 250 m each) and 6 halvings. A ridge thinner than a step can be missed.

GROUND BASES. Dock: ship in a surface frame, Normal or Landed; the nearest ground site of that body; within site radius (250) + DOCK_RANGE (1,500) = 1,750 m of the pad centre; speed over the ground at most 120 m/s. The docked ship's anchor becomes the site id; dock and undock events go to the surface zone. Undock: placeAtSite at radius + 500 = 750 m from the pad centre, above it, in the surface frame, at rest, then the usual half turn. Market, services, missions, home, respawn and insurance are the unchanged station code. Collider: BASE_COLLIDER, which is GROUND_BASE_STRUCTURE with both cylinders carried on down to 500 m below the pad so that no contact pushes a ship downward; push-out, reflection and damage as at a station. Weapons are jammed in secure systems within 4 km (MASS_LOCK_RADIUS) of a pad.

NPC SHIPS. spawnNpc throws for a surface zone; its only caller (npc.ts populate) spawns only where findSite(zone) has a quota, and a surface zone has no site. Nothing but simulateShip changes an NPC's anchor, and the tick removes an NPC whose anchor is a surface anchor right after that step.

CLIENT VIEW. isFlying includes Landed (ticks, input, prediction, drawn; view.self is non-null). Own ship, entities, camera and velocities are turned by the anchor frame's rotation (identity outside surface frames and ground-site frames). zone and zoneRot are set in Normal and Landed. `surface` is present while the camera is within 3 radii of the centre of a landable body (nearest ground wins). Camera: chase and wreck cameras are raised to 2 m above the terrain, the docked camera to 60 m; the chase camera follows in system axes, so a frame change does not disturb it. Entity tracks survive Normal <-> Landed. fx.cruise is at least 0.02 in cruise. Leaving the page asks for confirmation in Normal and Cruise, not when landed.

FOLD TUNNEL (item 9). Cause: a cross-server jump hands off at once, the client connected within a few hundredths of a second and reset its state, so often no frame was ever built in the tunnel. Fix: Game.ts handoff waits FOLD_TUNNEL_TIME (7 s) before it connects, showing the same 0..1 progress as an in-sector jump, then pulses until the other server answers; a counter drops a wait that was overtaken by a disconnect. This applies to every handoff, warp gates included. The ticket lives 120 s.

HUD (functional entries only). The velocity marker is projected from self.vel. The dock prompt also shows in a surface frame, flying or landed, within 1,750 m of the nearest base of that body. The cruise-drop prompt for a ground base chosen as nav target shows while the camera is below surface.enter over that base's body, anywhere around the body.
names: contracts.ts FrameView.zone: Vec3 | null - origin of the zone's frame relative to the camera, system axes; in a surface frame the body centre; non-null in Normal and Landed

contracts.ts FrameView.zoneRot: Quat | null - turns the zone's axes into system axes (identity outside surface frames); null exactly when zone is null; an event is seen at zone + rotate(zoneRot, ev.at)
contracts.ts FrameView.surface: SurfaceView | null - the landable body whose centre is within 3 radii of the camera

contracts.ts SurfaceView { body, rot, cam, camHeight, ship } - body id; bodyRotation at view.time (body-fixed to system axes); camera in body-fixed axes in float64, metres from the centre; camera height above the ground; ship is null whenever view.self is null

contracts.ts SurfaceShipView { pos, height, verticalSpeed, groundSpeed, slope, landed, up, normal } - ship origin in body-fixed axes; height of the lowest point above ground (0 landed); m/s away from the centre; m/s along the turning ground; slope in radians over the landing footprint; FlightMode.Landed; up and ground normal as unit vectors in system axes
contracts.ts SelfView.vel: Vec3 - velocity relative to the anchor frame in system axes; zero at rest over the ground
contracts.ts SelfView.state - CAVEAT: raw simulation state; pos, vel and rot are in the axes of state.anchor, which turn with the body in a surface frame; use rel, vel, rot for anything drawn
contracts.ts EntityView.rel, vel, rot - system axes; vel is relative to the zone's frame
contracts.ts FrameView.self - non-null for a landed ship; FrameView.mode can be FlightMode.Landed (5)
contracts.ts FrameFx.cruise - never below 0.02 in cruise, so cruise > 0 means in cruise; FrameFx.fold rises 0..1 during a handoff too
game/surface.ts SURFACE_VIEW_RADII = 3, CAMERA_GROUND_CLEARANCE = 2 (m)
game/surface.ts ViewFrame { anchor, pos, rot } and viewFrame(sys, anchor, t, bodyStates?) - frame of any anchor; rot is null when its axes are system axes
game/surface.ts toSystem(f, v), toFrame(f, v), rotToSystem(f, q) - vectors and orientations between frame axes and system axes
game/surface.ts bodyFixed(sys, f, local, surface, bodyRot, bodyPos) - a point of any frame in the body-fixed axes of a body
game/surface.ts liftAboveGround(sys, f, local, clearance = 2) - raises a camera position above the terrain; chaseCamera(sys, f, shipPos, camRot, radius) - chase position, never below ground
game/surface.ts sceneryView(sys, t, f, camLocal, bodyStates) - { camSys, bodies, sites } of a view; frameUp(f, local) - straight up at a point
game/surface.ts surfaceView(sys, t, f, camLocal, bodyStates, ship | null) - builds FrameView.surface; the ship may be in any frame
dev/fakeView.ts makeView(FakeViewOptions) - anchor may now be a surface frame or ground site; fills zoneRot, surface and self.vel

dev/fakeView.ts makeSurfaceView(SurfaceViewOptions): { view, place } - a true view over a real landable body; options system, site, time, hour, east, north, lat, lon, height, landed, heading, pitch, speed, climb, since, hull, cameraMode, look, fov, input, fx, graphics, galaxy, targetId, navAnchor, dt, clock; throws for landed on ground steeper than 20 degrees

dev/fakeView.ts SurfacePlace { system, site, body, ground, time, hour, sunElevation, frame, camLocal, state, point(east, north, up), rel(pos), at(pos), standing(pos, heading) } - for adding entities and events at ground spots
dev/fakeView.ts findGroundBase(systems), solarHour(sys, body, dir, t), timeOfHour(sys, body, dir, t, hour)

dev page /dev/local.html?scene=surface - options: state=flying|landed, alt (m, default 40), east and north (m from the pad, default 220 east) or lat and lon (deg), tod (hours, default 10), heading, pitch (deg), speed, climb (m/s), rate (universe seconds per second), look=yaw,pitch (deg), base=<n>, extras=0, info=0
dev page options shared with the other scenes: hull, cam=chase|cockpit, t, q, bloom, parts, self=0, and the fx overrides cruise, fold, charge, kind, dil, heat, hit
dev page hooks: window.__view (last FrameView), window.__place (SurfacePlace), window.__clock, window.__ready (after 30 frames); the readout element #surface-info
render/local/fx/core.ts Frame.qx, qy, qz, qw - the zone orientation; Frame.zx, zy, zz and every Track are in zone axes; fx/index.ts turns the root of the effects part by it each frame
server game.ts inSpace(state) - Normal or Landed: in a zone, detectable, hittable
server game.ts SimObject.belly?, SimObject.resting? - rest height of an object's origin above ground (default radius); lying on the ground
server ground.ts zoneSurface(def, zone) - BodySurface of a surface zone or null
server ground.ts impactFraction(stats, impact) and IMPACT_REF_SPEED 10, IMPACT_REF_FRACTION 0.25, IMPACT_EXPONENT 1.5, IMPACT_SCALE_MIN 0.7, IMPACT_SCALE_MAX 1.6, IMPACT_EPISODE 1
server ground.ts BASE_COLLIDER, PadPose, padPose(site), collideBase(pad, pos, radius), baseCovering(surface, pos), groundRay(surface, origin, dir, maxDist)

REVIEWER, on LAND_MAX_SLOPE and LAND_MIN_UPRIGHT: Math.tan and Math.cos are not required to be correctly rounded, so engines may differ in the last bit. Node and Chrome are both V8 and agree; Firefox or Safari could have a limit one ulp off, which matters only for a touchdown within one ulp of the limit: the client would predict the other outcome for one snapshot and the server's state would correct it. It is not a new class of problem: the same step already uses Math.sin, cos, exp and pow (orbits.ts, math.ts, ship.ts). Writing the two limits as literals (0.36397023426620234 and 0.8660254037844387) would remove this one. Server-only Math.cbrt and Math.pow in impactFraction are never predicted by a client
